dimensions.note: One pattern recurs across three independently gated readings, and the later two test it against rivals: a personal craft taste offered to particular people while the gap between her taste and their reception stays open. B0204 shows authored costumes whose wearers were a little taken aback (B:P2-3), a question whether her sense can still earn recognition (D:P4) and inspiration from company that she does not hand over to it (G:P2-4). B0232 case 20 has her give handmade toys whose shapes others call creepy while she finds them cute (P1-P2). B0237 404000022 has her attribute patchwork and appliques to Sui and Makoto (P7-15), recall work and memories made together (P16-17) and frame future costumes as her own intention; the reading names B0204's distinctive style, mixed reception and limited cooking as live counterexamples to global mastery. D rather than E because this is distributed, rival-tested support, not a single located trait. Not C because no conditional rule, trigger or state guard is derived and every occurrence is a monologic address.

All three readings forbid ordering the occurrences: B0204 rules out a chronology in which the manager gradually completes her, B0232 synchronizes no message with another, and B0237 supplies no year or Main placement. B0237's recalled alterations, internship and overnight gathering are named memories, not tracked states. The earlier Rishuri chapters are context only and not enrolled.

Located register evidence is local: written dialect forms もろて, ぎょうさん, ほんま and 冗談やって (B0237 P16-19, read as one authored register that names no hometown), the message title 支配人、聞いてやー (B0232), the recurring zonorish coinage (B0204 D:P5, G title; B0237 P0-6 and close) and an unspecified written dialect (B0204 E). The readings otherwise paraphrase her Japanese. All voice cues (31 in B0204, 13 in B0237) are unheard, and B0232 carries no voice.

Ordinary conduct is mostly reported or proposed: miso soup offered at a picnic with a named cooking limit (B0204 A), a shopping-street walk in which her attention moves to textiles (F), a gift practice of handmade toys answering received favours (B0232 P0-P2), and appreciation of a cake too characteristic to eat (B0237 P0-6). No cooking, sewing, eating or routine is enacted.

Rishuri addresses the manager in every reading, and his answers come only through her uptake (B0204 C:P3). B0237 adds a collective thanks to the preparers and attributed peer makers (Sui, Makoto, 七花少女), and B0232 a reported school friend; none has a turn. A conditional hometown pretense (B0204 E) and one represented hand contact (F) are both addressed to the same silent person. Two addressee positions do not support recipient conditioning.

Interior states are spoken self-reports: thinking about sewing while others talk and not matching their pace (B0204 C:P2), asking whether her sense can win recognition (D:P4), eyes easily drawn elsewhere (F), finding her gifts cute against others' appraisal (B0232 P1) and enjoyment of a recognizable world (B0237). No inward narration is distinguished from speech.

No disagreement or interpersonal conflict involving Rishuri is analyzed in the three readings. The drama club's reported hesitation and the creepy appraisal are differences in reception, not enacted disputes. Absence here is not evidence that she avoids conflict.

Returning a handmade toy for juice (B0232 P0) is reciprocity the reading declines to price, and the hometown boyfriend pretense (B0204 E) is a conditional social plan, not analyzed moral reasoning. Nothing is established about her ethical deliberation.

Two located instances of play: the laundry-set tease that she immediately calls a joke and tells the manager not to be flustered by (B0237 P18-19), which the reading treats as testing and withdrawing a service meaning; and the conditional proposal to pass the manager off as her boyfriend, with a request that he not improvise strangely (B0204 E:P4-5). Both are single-occurrence and addressed to one silent interlocutor.

Each curated unit is complete with exact native review: B0204's seven occurrences, B0232's three-page message and B0237's 22-page Birthday portfolio. Together they are still nine short, single-speaker occurrences. The earlier Main and i-n-g readings (B0099, B0129, B0137, B0140, B0175) are not enrolled, and no performed audio, loop movie or runtime was reviewed.

Affirmative local limits are located in all three readings: a named limit in what she can cook (B0204 A:P1-2), costume wearers reported as taken aback (B:P2-3), toy shapes reported as creepy (B0232 P1), and a service reading of the laundry gift withdrawn as a joke (B0237 P18-19). Each limit is case-local, so D is not supported.

The readings establish that no chronology, calendar or unlock level orders the occurrences. The only explicit markers are local: a coming holiday (B0204 E), today's aquarium trip (G), a prior juice gift locally ordered before the toy (B0232 P0) and a birthday of unstated year (B0237).

A reported picnic offer, a shopping walk, a gift practice and a received birthday party answer bounded canon questions about these occurrences, but give no procedure for an unfamiliar ordinary situation.

B0204 E's boyfriend role is an explicitly conditional pretense, F's hand contact is one represented local touch that the reading says establishes no reciprocal commitment, and C's daily thought of the manager is a self-report beside a conjecture about others. B0237 reads the laundry tease as withdrawn and supplies no settled romance. The evidence cannot support simulating a romance.

Costume design for a school play (B0204 B), fashion as a model for idol recognition (D) and anticipated costume development from gifts (B0237 P0-6) are her reports and intentions. No sewing, fitting, idol work or performance is shown, and the drama club's reception is only reported.

known_limits.statement: The nine sources are independent conditional occurrences with no chronology, year or unlock level; menu, catalog or execution order cannot make any occurrence a step in her development, and cross-case comparisons are thematic.

The drama club's hesitation, the creepy appraisal of her toys and the friend who could not look away are Rishuri's reports. They are neither an objective verdict on her craft nor evidence of universal welcome.
The hometown boyfriend role in B0204 E is conditional on a hypothetical request and an unrealized trip. It is not a past or present partner, a witnessed deception or the manager's assent.
The laundry-set remark in B0237 P18-19 is called a joke by Rishuri herself and must not be treated as an accepted chore, a domestic role or a manager motive.
Sui, Makoto, 七花少女, the school friend, the drama club and the sewing teacher enter only through her attribution or report; none has a turn, and no construction process is shown.
The play, ticket shift, hometown visit, patchwork experiment, Nanasta-wide gift distribution and future costumes are plans or intentions. None is completed in the curated evidence.
No performed voice, singing, music, loop movie or continuous runtime was heard or watched. Static craft-themed sprites, floating tools and stand art are not performances or observed sewing.
The earlier Rishuri readings (B0099, B0129, B0137, B0140, B0175) are not curated on this subject, so the readings' comparisons with them were not checked. Missing support is not evidence of absence.

Apart from a few written dialect forms, the zonorish coinage and short quotations, the readings paraphrase Rishuri's Japanese, so self-reference and sentence endings are largely absent from the curated evidence.

dimensions.note: The reading's cumulative finding is personal style widened through selected relations: hospitality offered with a named cooking limit (A:P1-P3), authorial pride in costumes whose wearers she reports as taken aback (B:P2-P3), a question whether her distinctive sense can earn recognition answered by chosen self-encouragement (D:P4-P5), and company requested so that material curiosity can continue (F:P4-P5, G:P4). The pattern recurs across five addresses, but each address is three to five pages and no conditional rule is derived, so D is not supported; it is more than one located trait, so it is graded rather than NOT_ASSESSED.

The reading affirmatively forbids ordering the seven occurrences and denies a progression of mutual romance or of the manager completing her. Earlier Rishuri states (B0099-B0175) are context only and not enrolled. No change is tracked beyond a few pages.

Very little register is located: the characteristic phrase zonorish legend (D:P5), her self-description of the stage as Rishuri-produced (B:P2) and a passing reference to written dialect (E). Otherwise the reading paraphrases her Japanese, and the 31 voice cues were not heard, so self-reference, sentence endings and delivery are not in evidence.

Ordinary activities are mostly reported rather than shown: miso soup brought to a picnic (A), planned ticket-desk work (B:P4), noticing slippers, cushions and pillowcases on a shopping-street walk (F:P1-P3) and an aquarium trip that prompts a patchwork idea (G:P1-P3). Only F represents a present local exchange; there is no enacted routine.

Nearly all evidence is Rishuri addressing the manager, whose replies reach the reader only through her uptake. The drama club, the neighborhood sewing teacher, Nanasta peers and Nicole appear only in her reports, and the reading declines to supply their interiors or reception. One relation does not support recipient conditioning.

Interior states are spoken self-reports: thinking about sewing while others talk and not following the topic (C:P2), thinking about the manager every day (C:P4-P5), and doubt whether her sense can win recognition (D:P4). The reading keeps her estimate of others' minds (everyone surely thinks of him too) distinct from evidence of them. No inward narration is distinguished from speech.

No disagreement or interpersonal conflict involving Rishuri is analyzed. The club members' reported hesitancy (B:P2-P3) is reception she describes, not conflict, and absence is not evidence that she avoids conflict.

The conditional boyfriend pretense (E:P4-P5) is read as an imagined social role with a performance limit, not analyzed as ethical reasoning about deception. Nothing is established about her ethical deliberation.
The reading describes her choice of the manager for the pretense as playful (E) but analyzes no joking or play as such. One descriptive word does not establish humor evidence.

The family is complete: seven occurrences with exact scripts and hashes, all 31 Japanese and name records and 38 native objects read, one composite and five backgrounds viewed, and 66 context rows compared. It is still seven short addresses; the earlier Main and i-n-g readings are not enrolled, and no performed audio or runtime was reviewed.

Affirmative limits are located: she names cooking as a domain of less confidence (A:P1-P2), says she often does not understand peers' topics or match their pace (C:P2), reports the club members as taken aback by her costumes (B:P2-P3), and her legend is a future wish, not achieved recognition (D:P5). The reading also denies a finished patchwork design (G).
The reading establishes that no chronology, calendar or unlock level orders the occurrences. The upcoming holiday (E) and today's aquarium trip (G) are local to their own addresses.
